issues: Recurrent early evening (18:00-19:00) and overnight (23:00-03:00) hypoglycemia.
100% reliance on Unannounced Meals (UAM) does not account for the delayed gastric emptying caused by GLP-1 medication.
The max_iob_units limit is set to an unusually high 25 U, posing a significant overdose risk if a false CGM high occurs.
The overnight target of 90 mg/dL provides almost no safety buffer against UAM and Dynamic ISF overcorrections.
summary: The profile demonstrates excellent overall Time in Range (86%) achieved through a completely unannounced meal (UAM) strategy combined with Dynamic ISF. However, the lack of carbohydrate logging paired with GLP-1 delayed digestion causes the algorithm to aggressively stack insulin during slow glucose rises, resulting in recurrent and significant evening and overnight hypoglycemia.
education: GLP-1 medications significantly slow gastric emptying. This means food takes much longer to raise blood glucose compared to standard digestion.

Unannounced Meal (UAM) algorithms react only to rising glucose. If glucose rises slowly but steadily over many hours (due to GLP-1), UAM may continually stack insulin (SMBs), which can lead to hypoglycemia when the stacked insulin finally peaks against the slow food absorption.
Raising the glucose target during sleep provides a physical safety buffer that prevents automated systems from delivering micro-boluses too close to the hypoglycemia threshold.
strengths: Exceptional Time in Range (86.0%) and Time Above Range control (8.9%).
Highly stable fasting glucose patterns between 04:00 and 07:00 when meals are not impacting the system.
Consistent sensor usage with 98.7% CGM coverage over the 14-day period.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.

The 'max_iob_units' is currently set to 25 U. For a profile with a total daily basal of roughly 16 U, this is exceptionally high. Discuss reducing this safety ceiling with your care team immediately to prevent severe accidental overdosing in the event of a sensor error or prolonged resistance.

analysis_steps.evidence: 14-day range with 98.7% CGM coverage. 3,995 valid entries. 0 logged carbohydrates. 'GLP-1 1.25mg' annotated.
analysis_steps.findings: CGM tracking is exceptionally stable. The total lack of logged carbohydrate entries indicates the user is relying entirely on unannounced meals (UAM).
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete absence of meal composition and meal timing records limits traditional CR and precise absorption evaluation.

analysis_steps.evidence: Time Below Range is 5.1%. Extreme lows (41-48 mg/dL) documented. Hourly local data shows concentrated hypoglycemia overnight (23:00-03:00) and early evening (18:00-19:00).
analysis_steps.findings: The primary safety concern is the recurring, clustered nighttime and evening hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot directly verify if the 18:00-19:00 lows immediately follow meals due to the lack of carb logging.

analysis_steps.evidence: Target drops to 90 mg/dL from 23:00 to 08:00. Fasting/morning hours (04:00-07:00) show stable glucose (~100 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.findings: The 90 mg/dL target overnight leaves very little safety buffer for an automated system generating SMBs. Fasting hours are tuned well, but the 23:00-03:00 phase is plagued by lows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Uncertainty around whether 18:00-19:00 lows are purely basal-driven or a rebound from automated corrections applied to an unlogged afternoon meal.

analysis_steps.evidence: DIA is 10 hours. Flat ISF at 56 mg/dL/U. Tiny correction boluses create massive drops (e.g., 0.2U dropped BG by 178 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.findings: A flat ISF combined with Dynamic ISF adjustments leads to aggressive overtreatment of late-afternoon highs, which subsequently plunge into the 18:00-19:00 lows.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Without carb entries, Carb Ratios cannot be independently validated against specific meals.

analysis_steps.findings: Automation settings perfectly align with the zero-carb-logged reality. The 3-minute interval allows incredibly fast action on CGM deviations, treating all post-meal spikes as pure UAM deviations.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None regarding settings, though lack of meal logging limits visibility into the exact delay between eating and the UAM response.

analysis_steps.evidence: dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true. variable_sens swings from 124 down to 27.8 mg/dL/U. max_iob_units is 25 U.
analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF shrinks the ISF to as low as 27.8 mg/dL/U during highs, authorizing vastly stronger SMBs. The max_iob_units of 25 U removes the intended mechanical ceiling for safety.

analysis_steps.evidence: 0 logged carbohydrates, 0 extended carbs. Occasional manual correction boluses.
analysis_steps.findings: There is no declared prebolus time, immediate bolus percentage, or conventional meal announcement. The user relies entirely on reactive UAM.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of meal timing and composition data prevents calculation of exact insulin-to-carb efficacy.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs are not being utilized. AAPS has no mechanical way to anticipate the delayed absorption curve of the GLP-1 medication because no meals are entered.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None regarding settings execution, as the feature is completely unused.

analysis_steps.evidence: Combined package data, GLP-1 annotations, UAM execution, and recurring hypoglycemia clusters.
analysis_steps.findings: The safest immediate intervention is raising the nighttime target to 100 mg/dL to prevent aggressive UAM stacking near the hypoglycemia threshold. Long-term safety requires addressing the 25 U max_iob limit and implementing carb logging to manage GLP-1 delays.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: None blocking the immediate target change.

recommendations.title: Raise overnight target
recommendations.description: The 90 mg/dL overnight target provides insufficient buffer against UAM-driven insulin stacking, directly contributing to the 23:00-03:00 lows.

recommendations.title: Review Max IOB
recommendations.description: A max IOB of 25 U is severely disproportional to a ~16 U total daily basal and 56 mg/dL/U ISF, risking severe hypoglycemia.

recommendations.title: Log Carbohydrates
recommendations.description: Logging carbohydrates, even as rough estimates or e-carbs, provides the algorithm with critical forward-looking context for GLP-1 delayed absorption, reducing reactive UAM over-corrections.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Raising the 23:00 and 00:00 targets to 100 mg/dL establishes a safer baseline during sleep, preventing Dynamic ISF and UAM from issuing micro-boluses too close to the hypoglycemia threshold.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Observe overnight glucose for 3-5 days to confirm Time Below Range drops below 4%.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Change the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.

implementation_steps: Discuss the extremely high max_iob_units (25 U) setting with the care team immediately to prevent severe accidental overdosing.
Raise the 23:00 and 00:00 targets from 90 to 100 mg/dL to establish a safer baseline against overnight UAM corrections.
Begin logging carbohydrate amounts for meals, particularly dinner, to give the algorithm visibility into approaching glucose rises.
Evaluate if e-carbs better match the GLP-1 delayed absorption after establishing a baseline of logged meals.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user relies entirely on UAM with zero logged carbs. GLP-1 slows digestion, leading UAM to stack insulin reactively early on and cause later hypoglycemia when the insulin outpaces the delayed absorption.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Begin logging carbohydrate estimates for meals to map the delayed GLP-1 absorption curve into AAPS, transitioning away from a 100% reactive UAM strategy.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log dinner carbohydrates for 3 days and observe if 18:00-19:00 and 23:00-03:00 lows decrease.
